eval_critique: Assertions 1-6 and 8-10 were all satisfied by both configurations, so eval-1 did not discriminate in this iteration; the baseline model already knows the Iterate/Load-once and Insert-or-update/batch facts.

Assertion 7 ('does not invent components or settings') is a negative check that passes by default unless the grader catches a fabrication; it cannot distinguish a careful answer from a lucky one. Consider replacing it with a positive spot-check (e.g. 'states tLogRow_2 is deactivated', 'states tMap_1 Die on error is ON while tDBOutput_1/tFileInputDelimited_1 are OFF', 'states customer_id is Update key and not updatable').

No assertion checks the PostgreSQL aborted-transaction consequence of Die-on-error-off with autocommit off (first failed statement poisons the transaction so the final COMMIT behaves as rollback), which only one answer raised and which is the most production-relevant finding.

No assertion covers the email-filter silent drop (out_ok filter with no Catch output reject), the deactivated tLogRow_2 reject target, or the misleading tDie message ('Load failed: null'); all are concrete facts in the XML that a weaker answer would miss.

The prompt says 'the only thing I have is the exported item file' but both answers also read LOAD_CUSTOMERS_0.1.properties from the fixtures directory; if the eval intends item-only analysis, the fixture folder should not contain the .properties file.
